messages:
Akshay (customer): Hey team — after we moved our Dedicated instance into our VPC behind an AWS ALB, auth started failing intermittently. Small requests OK, but when our SSO token is large (long JWT), calls return 401 from ext_authz. No code change on our side.

Maya (support): Ugh. Thanks for the heads up — can you paste a failing request (with token redacted) and any error logs from the gateway/ext_authz? Also which ALB type (classic/ALB/NLB) and HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2?

Akshay (customer): ALB (application). Using HTTP/1.1. We have the edge-proxy that rewrites our signed cookie `session_jwt` into `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` before forwarding to internal Envoy. Failing curl (token replaced with <JWT_REDACTED>):

```
curl -v -H "Host: api.customer.example" \\
  -H "Cookie: session_jwt=<JWT_REDACTED>" \\
  https://dedicated.customer.example/v1/generate
```

Response header: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and body: `{"error":"missing authorization header"}`.

I grabbed the edge-proxy logs (redacted):

```
[2024-11-20T16:12:03Z] rewrite: cookie->Authorization set; len=8743
[2024-11-20T16:12:03Z] forward to ALB: headers: authorization: Bearer <part1>
authorization: <part2>
authorization: <part3>
[2024-11-20T16:12:03Z] response from internal: 401 ext_authz: token parse failed
```

Maya (support): That log line where ALB shows multiple `authorization` header lines stands out. ALB has header size/line length behavior and proxies sometimes split long headers. Envoy/ext_authz may only look at the first header line or drop when token is split.

Devon (eng-platform): Yep — we saw this before. ALB can fragment long headers into multiple header lines when they exceed internal limits. Envoy will merge header lines but our ext_authz filter expects a single contiguous `Authorization` header with `Bearer <token>`. If ALB splits it into multiple lines, some filters downstream treat it as malformed.

Lina (eng-infra): Quick checks: 1) confirm `Authorization` arrives to Envoy as one header (curl to internal directly), 2) check Envoy `max_request_headers_kb` and `headers_with_underscores_action` config, 3) verify ALB/proxy doesn't inject chunked header lines.

Akshay (customer): I tried curling the internal envoy directly from inside the VPC (bypassing ALB) and it succeeds:

```
curl -v -H "Host: api.customer.example" -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT_REDACTED>" https://internal.envoy.local/v1/generate
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

So confirms ALB/proxy is altering it. Any quick workaround? We can't change token size immediately.

Devon (eng-platform): Workarounds: 1) Have edge-proxy send token in the request body or as a shorter session id (requires app change). 2) Configure edge-proxy to send `Authorization` as multiple shorter headers is bad — instead reassemble before ALB (hard). 3) Temporary: enable cookie-based auth in the internal gateway so it reads `session_jwt` cookie directly instead of relying on rewritten `Authorization`. That avoids the long header in the request path.

Maya (support): For a repro from our side, can you run a small test that simulates ALB fragmentation locally? Example (simulate split headers):

```
# python quick server that sends multiple Authorization header lines
curl -v -H "Host: api.customer.example" -H "Authorization: Bearer part1" -H "Authorization: part2" https://internal.envoy.local/v1/generate
```

If that reproduces 401, we know ext_authz chokes on split lines.

Lina (eng-infra): On Envoy we can bump `max_request_headers_kb` (default 60KB) and ensure `allow_chunked_length` not enabled. But this is risky cluster-wide. Better short term: update our dedicated-edge config to preserve the cookie and add a rule in the internal auth filter that checks `Cookie: session_jwt` if `Authorization` missing or malformed.

Devon (eng-platform): Also check ALB docs — sometimes converting to HTTP/2 between ALB and backend or switching to NLB + TLS passthrough stops header reformatting. If ALB is rewrapping, using NLB/TCP passthrough to Envoy may avoid fragmentation.

Akshay (customer): I applied a quick patch to the internal auth filter to fallback to cookie parsing and that fixed the customer request immediately (no app changes). Good temporary fix.

ops-bot: Deployment notice — config change `auth/fallback-cookie` rolled out to dedicated cluster staging -> production at 2024-11-20T18:02:11Z by Devon. :rocket:

Maya (support): Notes for the support ticket and postmortem: root cause: ALB/application layer splitting very large `Authorization` headers (long JWTs) into multiple header lines; ext_authz expected a single contiguous header.

Action items:
- Devon (eng-platform): follow up PR to add opt-in cookie fallback in internal auth filter and tests for multi-line Authorization (owner).
- Lina (eng-infra): evaluate cluster-level Envoy header buffer tweaks vs risk for memory, and verify NLB passthrough as alternative (owner).
- Maya (support): provide customer with mitigation steps (use cookie fallback, or shorten token) and update KB.

Devon (eng-platform): I'll open the PR. Short-term recommendation to customers: avoid putting huge JWTs into Authorization if possible; if not, use cookie-based forwarding or an NLB/TLS passthrough.

Akshay (customer): Thanks all — the fallback helped and we're coordinating to reduce token size longer-term. Appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:

Maya (support): Closing loop here — I'll mark the ticket resolved once customer confirms stable for 24h. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
